title: Multi-state capture histories (juvenile, immature/unknown, breeder) of 102 female serotine bats at the Hollingbury maternity roost, England, 1989-2011
creator: Chauvenet, Aliénor L. M.; Hutson, Anthony M.; Smith, Graham C.; Aegerter, James N.
citation: Chauvenet, A. L. M., Hutson, A. M., Smith, G. C., & Aegerter, J. N. (2014). Data from: Demographic variation in the U.K. serotine bat: filling gaps in knowledge for management [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.6kp2j
abstract: Female serotine bats (Eptesicus serotinus) ringed and recaptured at the Hollingbury maternity roost in south-east England in 12 capture years between 1989 and 2011, each capture assigned to a life stage (juvenile, immature/unknown, breeder). The authors fitted multistate CJS and POPAN models to estimate stage-specific survival, transitions and abundance.
samplingProtocol: Annual or ad hoc capture visits to a maternity roost (usually twice between May and August, or once in August), bats caught by hand in the roost or with hand nets / harp traps outside, ringed, aged by ossification and assessed for breeding; captures pooled to one annual occasion per year.

stateCodes.2: caught as immature or unknown stage (U: adult-looking, breeding not recorded or not determinable)

closureNote: one annual occasion per capture year (visits within a year pooled by the authors); capture years are unevenly spaced (__periods)
geographicCoverage: Hollingbury, Brighton, East Sussex, England (roof void of a former golf clubhouse)

notShipped.popan_files: the POPAN 0/1 histories: the MS histories with J/U/B recoded to 1 (asserted)
notShipped.mark_projects: MARK .DBF / .FPT project files and model results
notShipped.males: males, excluded by the authors and not deposited

notes: Females only. A female first caught as a juvenile has rows from that year; one first caught as U or B from the first capture year (E4.4). The authors assumed a bat once recorded as a breeder stays a breeder; U after B occurs in the data as recorded (y_raw).
